 Amid looming dry spell Cebu province prepares anti-dengue measures
 Jonnavie Villa - The Freeman October 24, 2026 | 12:00am 
 CEBU, Philippines — The need to store water amid a looming dry spell could increase the risk of dengue in Cebu, prompting the Provincial Health Office (PHO) to include mosquito control in its Super El Niño response plan.
 Provincial Health Officer Dr. Sheila Faciol said mosquito control is among the priorities of the province’s El Niño health response plan, as prolonged dry conditions could force residents to store water for household consumption.
 “Cover lang gyud ang tanan-tanan gipundo nga tubig, tabunan gyud siya, para dili mangitlog ang lamok,” said Faciol.
 She urged households to keep stored water containers covered to prevent mosquitoes from laying eggs.
 The PHO is also preparing interventions against heat-related illnesses and waterborne diseases, which may become more prevalent during prolonged dry spells and water shortages.
 Faciol said the health response plan would be organized into four clusters: medical services; water, sanitation and hygiene; nutrition; and mental health.
 Under the medical services cluster, the PHO is preparing to address illnesses such as diarrhea and heat-related conditions, including heat exhaustion and heatstroke.
 The office is considering providing cooling pads, oral rehydration solutions and intravenous fluids for patients who require medical treatment.
 The PHO is also concerned about waterborne diseases resulting from the consumption of unsafe drinking water, particularly as residents seek alternative water sources during shortages.
 To address this concern, the office plans to distribute water-purification tablets and 20-liter jerrycans for drinking water. Each container can hold the amount of water that can be treated with one tablet, Faciol said.
 “The concern nato sa health would be the safety of the water nga imnon sa mga tawo, the potability ba,” she said, emphasizing the importance of ensuring that stored water is safe for consumption.
 The nutrition cluster will focus on providing energy-rich and nutritious food, while the mental health cluster will address possible psychological concerns arising from the emergency.
 The province also plans to coordinate with local government units (LGUs) in distributing supplies, with the PHO supplementing the preparations of municipal and city health offices.
 The province’s 16 hospitals are likewise preparing their respective El Niño response plans, which Faciol said she was awaiting.
 Aside from mosquito-borne and waterborne diseases, the PHO is monitoring the risk of heat-related illnesses as temperatures rise and water sources potentially dry up.
 Faciol urged residents to prepare for possible water shortages while taking precautions when storing water and ensuring that drinking water remains safe for consumption.
 She said the province’s health preparations would focus on heat-related illnesses, waterborne diseases and mosquito-borne diseases as it anticipates the effects of Super El Niño. — /IHM (FREEMAN)
